result.topic_en: Pages 206–207: Euler takes particular values of ω and n in his interpolation series for sines. He derives series for sin ωπ when n = 1/2. He then compares this with an earlier solution that gives a series in 1/((k±n)^2−ω^2). From it he deduces 1 − 1/4 + 1/9 − 1/16 + … = π²/12 and the sum of 1/(k²−ω²) with alternating signs.
result.transcription:
206
Sumamus hic $\omega=\frac{1}{2}$, fiet:
$\frac{1}{4}[?]=1-\frac{1.1.1}{1.1.2.3^2}[?]-\frac{1.1.1.3.3.1}{1.1.2.2.3.3.5^2}[?]-\text{etc.}$
quae posterior series ita referri potest:
$-\frac{1}{3^2}-\frac{1.1.1}{1.1.2.5^2}[?]-\frac{1.1.3.3.5}{1.1.2.2.3.3.7^2}[?]-\text{etc.}$
Corollarium 3.
§. 55. Si fuerit $n=\frac{1}{2}$, vt sit $\sin.n\pi=1$, erunt factores, ex quibus singulos seriei terminos formari oportet:
$\frac{2\omega}{1},\ \frac{1-4\omega\omega}{1.2}[?],\ \frac{1-4\omega\omega}{3.4}[?],\ \frac{9-4\omega\omega}{5.6}[?],\ \frac{9-4\omega\omega}{7.8}[?],\ \frac{25-4\omega\omega}{9.10}[?],\ \text{etc.}$
atque seriei summa erit $\sin.\omega\pi$, scilicet:
$\sin.\omega\pi=2\omega+\frac{2\omega(1-4\omega\omega)}{1.2}+\frac{2\omega(1-4\omega\omega)^2}{1.2.3.4}+\frac{2\omega(1-4\omega\omega)^2(9-4\omega\omega)}{1.2.3.4.5.6}+\text{etc.}$
vnde, sumto $\omega=1$, esse debet:
$0=2-3+\frac{3}{2^3}[?]+\frac{5}{2^3.3}[?]+\frac{5}{2^4.5}[?]+\frac{7}{2^5.5}[?]+\frac{7}{2^6.7}[?]+\frac{9}{2^7.7}[?]+\frac{5.9}{2^8.7}[?]+\text{etc.}$
cuius veritas calculum instituenti mox patebit.
Scholion.
§. 56. Pro hoc casu etiam solutio supra inventa attentius considerari meretur, quae ex §. 36. ob
$\Delta=\frac{(n-\omega)\pi\sin.n\pi\sin.\omega\pi}{n\omega\sin.(n-\omega)\pi\sin.(n+\omega)\pi}[?]$ et $y=\frac{f\sin.\omega\pi}{\sin.n\pi}[?]$,
cum sit $p=f,\ q=f,\ r=-f,\ s=-f,\ t=f,\ u=f$ etc. in hac continetur aequatione:
$\frac{\pi\sin.n\pi\sin.\omega\pi}{\omega\sin.(n-\omega)\pi\sin.(n+\omega)\pi}=\frac{1}{nn-\omega\omega}-\frac{1}{(1-n)^2-\omega^2}-\frac{1}{(1+n)^2-\omega^2}+\frac{1}{(2-n)^2-\omega^2}+\frac{1}{(2+n)^2-\omega^2}-\text{etc.}$
quae series maxime discrepat ab ea, quam modo inuenimus. Circa hanc autem seriem sequentia obseruo.
I. Si

207
I. Si $\omega$ euanescat, fore
$\frac{\pi\pi\cos.n\pi}{(\sin.n\pi)^2}=\frac{1}{nn}-\frac{1}{(1-n)^2}-\frac{1}{(1+n)^2}+\frac{1}{(2-n)^2}+\frac{1}{(2+n)^2}-\text{etc.}$
at si insuper $n$ euanescat, ob $\sin.n\pi=n\pi$ incommodum nasci sequens:
$\frac{1}{nn}=\frac{1}{nn}-\frac{2}{1}+\frac{2}{4}-\frac{2}{9}+\frac{2}{16}-\text{etc.}$
Ad hoc autem tollendum, numerum $n$ vt tantum non euanescentem spectemus, et cum sit $\cos.n\pi=1-\frac{1}{2}nn\pi\pi$ et $\sin.n\pi=n\pi-\frac{1}{6}n^3\pi^3=n\pi(1-\frac{1}{6}nn\pi\pi)$, erit
$\frac{\cos.n\pi}{(\sin.n\pi)^2}=\frac{1-\frac{1}{2}nn\pi\pi}{nn\pi\pi(1-\frac{1}{3}nn\pi\pi)}=\frac{1-\frac{1}{6}nn\pi\pi}{nn\pi\pi}$,
vnde obtinetur haec vera aequatio:
$\frac{1}{nn}-\frac{1}{6}\pi\pi=\frac{1}{nn}-\frac{2}{1}+\frac{2}{4}-\frac{2}{9}+\frac{2}{16}-\frac{2}{25}+\text{etc.}$
Est enim
$1-\frac{1}{4}+\frac{1}{9}-\frac{1}{16}+\frac{1}{25}-\text{etc.}=\frac{1}{12}\pi\pi.$
II. Ponamus nunc $n=0$ et habebimus:
$-\frac{\pi}{\omega\sin.\omega\pi}=-\frac{1}{\omega^2}-\frac{1}{1-\omega^2}-\frac{1}{1-\omega^2}+\frac{1}{4-\omega^2}+\frac{1}{4-\omega^2}-\frac{1}{9-\omega^2}-\frac{1}{9-\omega^2}-\text{etc.}$
seu $\frac{\pi}{\omega\sin.\omega\pi}=\frac{1}{\omega^2}+\frac{2}{1-\omega^2}-\frac{2}{4-\omega^2}+\frac{2}{9-\omega^2}-\frac{2}{16-\omega^2}+\frac{2}{25-\omega^2}-\text{etc.}$
vnde consequimur hanc memorabilem summationem:
$\frac{1}{1-\omega^2}-\frac{1}{4-\omega^2}+\frac{1}{9-\omega^2}-\frac{1}{16-\omega^2}+\text{etc.}=\frac{\pi}{2\omega\sin.\omega\pi}-\frac{1}{2\omega\omega}$,
cuius veritatem alibi demonstratam dedi. Hinc autem, sumto $\omega$ infinite paruo, ob $\sin.\omega\pi=\omega\pi(1-\frac{1}{6}\omega^2\pi^2)$ seriei
$1-\frac{1}{4}+\frac{1}{9}-\frac{1}{16}+\frac{1}{25}-\text{etc.}$ summa vt ante colligitur:
$\frac{1}{2\omega\omega(1-\frac{1}{6}\omega^2\pi^2)}-\frac{1}{2\omega\omega}=\frac{1}{12}\pi\pi.$
III.
